The Renaissance in Florence

The Italian Renaissance began in Florence in the 14th century, driven by the wealth of the Medici family and a revival of classical learning. Artists such as Giotto and later Brunelleschi transformed architecture and painting.

Humanist scholars rediscovered ancient Greek and Roman texts, and the invention of movable type by Gutenberg around 1450 helped spread ideas across Europe.

Florence's Duomo, completed in 1436, remains an engineering marvel of its era.
